hero_title: Your next video. Your old Xbox.
hero_description: YouTube, native on Xbox 360. Open source. Built for your controller.
tv_label: Interactive Tube360 preview. Use arrow keys to select a video, Enter to watch and Escape to go back.
desktop_help: arrow keys, click or a controller
mobile_help: tap a video or use the controls below
down: Select below or open Like / Dislike
disclosure: A hands-on preview of the interface. The app itself runs on your Xbox 360.
how_title_1: A little help from your PC.
how_description: A small server converts the video on the fly. Tube360 receives it over your home network and decodes it on the console’s own CPU.
server_node: Node.js for Cast and your account
decoding: 720p at 30 fps, decoded on the CPU
footprint_description: About 140 MB RAM and ~0% CPU while idle. Playing 720p uses around three quarters of one CPU core.
server_options: The server can also run on a small VPS or an old Android phone.
features_intro_1: Your videos, your account, your controller.
features_intro_2: With a few good reasons to stay on the sofa.
account_description: Sign in once with a TV code. Recommendations, subscriptions, continue watching and Watch later. Your history stays with your account.
search_description: Browse categories and a home grid with three or four videos per row. Search with the on-screen keyboard, all from your controller.
cast_title: Your phone can take the lead
cast_description: Use the normal Cast button in the official YouTube app. Send sound to a Google Nest or Chromecast speaker, in sync with the picture.
sleep_title: One less thing to switch off
sleep_description: Set a sleep timer. Tube360 turns off the Xbox when it’s time, and the PC too if you choose.
account_alt: Tube360 sign-in screen with a code for linking a YouTube account
account_caption: Sign in on the TV. Make yourself at home.
actual_interface: Actual Tube360 interface, captured on PC
player_description: Press down in the player to like or dislike without leaving the video.
maintenance_description: The server keeps yt-dlp up to date. Members-only videos stay out of the grid, and playback refusals tell you why.
language_description: Use the interface in English or Portuguese, with familiar Xbox One / Series style button prompts.
install_intro: A native app, a small server, and your home network.
requirements_console: An Xbox 360 that runs unsigned code.
requirements_hacks: BadUpdate, RGH or JTAG. Tested with BadUpdate + XeUnshackle + Aurora.
requirements_software: Linux, tested on Fedora. Python 3.11+, ffmpeg and Node.js 22+.
requirements_other: The Python server should also run on macOS and Windows; the service scripts use systemd.
step_1_description: Set up the Python server on your PC. Add the Node.js service for your YouTube account and Cast.
step_2_description: Extract the ZIP and copy its Tube360 folder to Hdd1:\Games\ on the Xbox. Edit server.txt in that folder with your PC’s IP and port.
step_3_description: On Linux, install the services to start the server and Cast at login and keep yt-dlp updated. Launch from Aurora and sign in with the TV code.
star_description: If Tube360 is useful to you, a star on GitHub is the best thank-you.
legal: Tube360 is not affiliated with YouTube, Google or Microsoft. YouTube is a trademark of Google LLC. Xbox 360 is a trademark of Microsoft.
